decisions.reason: The candidate only permits use of the common website footer on informational pages; changing that footer's own background color does not alter the optional-reference requirement.
The footer background-color decision does not change the requirement to omit header navigation.
The client explicitly limits the dark-gray replacement to the footer, so the landing-page hero's purple background and other visual-design attributes remain unchanged.
The source selects a footer-specific background color but does not require a change to the design-token deliverables, documented token categories, or existing token preferences.
The provisioning wizard may optionally include the common footer, but the source does not change whether that footer is optional or any wizard-specific styling requirement.

The sign-in page may optionally include the common footer, but the footer's internal color change does not alter the page-treatment, branding, background, header-logo, or optional-footer requirements.
Changing the footer background color has no entailed effect on responsive layout behavior or breakpoint guidance.
The source concerns the public website footer, not the distinct dashboard or console shell footer and its light/dark-mode styling.
The footer color choice does not change the implementation stack, handoff objective, or handoff scope.
